questions.prompt: Which criterion establishes continuity of f from X to Y?
options: Every singleton image is open
f must preserve distances
For every open V in Y, its preimage under f is open in X
The image of every open set must be open
questions.answer_text: For every open V in Y, its preimage under f is open in X
questions.explanation: Continuity is defined by preimages of open sets, not open images.

questions.prompt: Which set is the closure of A in a topological space?
options: The set of isolated points of A
The smallest closed set containing A
The largest open set contained in A
The complement of A
questions.answer_text: The smallest closed set containing A
questions.explanation: Closure is the intersection of all closed supersets of A.

questions.prompt: Which property is necessary for a family B to be a basis for a topology?
options: At any point in the intersection of two basis sets, a third basis set contains that point and lies in the intersection
Every basis set is finite
Every subset of X lies in B
The basis must contain exactly one set
questions.answer_text: At any point in the intersection of two basis sets, a third basis set contains that point and lies in the intersection
questions.explanation: The basis intersection condition ensures finite intersections generate open sets.

questions.prompt: In the topology {empty, {a}, {a,b}} on {a,b}, which statement is true?
options: Both singleton sets are open
There is no nonempty open set
The topology is discrete
{b} is not open
questions.answer_text: {b} is not open
questions.explanation: The family contains {a} but not {b}, hence it is not discrete.

questions.prompt: In a metric space, what does d(x,y)=0 imply?
options: x and y have the same limit
The space is compact
x equals y
x and y lie in the same component only
questions.answer_text: x equals y
questions.explanation: Identity of indiscernibles is a metric axiom.

questions.prompt: Which hypothesis makes every Cauchy sequence converge within the space?
options: First countability alone
Completeness
Connectedness
Boundedness
questions.answer_text: Completeness
questions.explanation: Completeness is exactly convergence of every Cauchy sequence within the space.

questions.prompt: Two metrics generate the same open sets. What necessarily follows?
options: They induce the same topology
They have identical numerical distances
They have identical Cauchy sequences in general
They are scalar multiples
questions.answer_text: They induce the same topology
questions.explanation: Topological equivalence is equality of the induced open-set families.

questions.prompt: What does first countability require at a point x?
options: A countable total number of points
Every neighborhood to be finite
Only finitely many open sets
A countable neighborhood basis at x
questions.answer_text: A countable neighborhood basis at x
questions.explanation: The defining requirement is a countable local base at each point.

questions.prompt: What is the Hausdorff separation property?
options: Every sequence has a convergent subsequence
All open sets are closed
Distinct points admit disjoint open neighborhoods
Every closed set is compact
questions.answer_text: Distinct points admit disjoint open neighborhoods
questions.explanation: T2 separation means distinct points have disjoint neighborhoods.

questions.prompt: Which statement about every metric space is correct?
options: It is finite
It is Hausdorff
It is compact
It is connected
questions.answer_text: It is Hausdorff
questions.explanation: For distinct x,y, sufficiently small disjoint open balls separate them.

questions.prompt: Which statement defines compactness in a general topological space?
options: Every open cover has a finite subcover
Every subset is closed
Every Cauchy sequence converges
Every cover is countable
questions.answer_text: Every open cover has a finite subcover
questions.explanation: Compactness is the finite-subcover property for open covers.

questions.prompt: For a continuous f:X to Y, if X is compact then which set is compact?
options: All of Y
Every subset of Y
The preimage of any compact set without conditions
f(X)
questions.answer_text: f(X)
questions.explanation: A continuous image of a compact space is compact.

questions.prompt: How is connectedness characterized by open sets?
options: Every open cover has a finite subcover
Every singleton is closed
The space cannot be partitioned into two disjoint nonempty open sets
All points are joined by a straight segment
questions.answer_text: The space cannot be partitioned into two disjoint nonempty open sets
questions.explanation: A separation by two disjoint nonempty open sets contradicts connectedness.

questions.prompt: Which implication always holds?
options: Hausdorff implies connected
Path connected implies connected
Connected implies path connected
Compact implies path connected
questions.answer_text: Path connected implies connected
questions.explanation: A continuous path cannot separate into disconnected image pieces; converses need not hold.

questions.prompt: Which map is always continuous for the product topology on X times Y?
options: The coordinate projection to X
Every map from X times Y to any space
Every surjection from X times Y
A projection from an arbitrary quotient topology
questions.answer_text: The coordinate projection to X
questions.explanation: The product topology is defined so coordinate projections are continuous.

questions.prompt: For quotient map q:X to Y, which criterion characterizes an open U subset of Y?
options: Its image under q is open in X
Its preimage must be closed
U must be finite
Its preimage under q is open in X
questions.answer_text: Its preimage under q is open in X
questions.explanation: The quotient topology is exactly the family whose inverse images under q are open.

questions.prompt: What is a homotopy between maps f and g from X to Y?
options: A metric-preserving map
A sequence of disconnected maps
A continuous H from X times [0,1] to Y with endpoints f and g
An arbitrary pointwise bijection between X and Y
questions.answer_text: A continuous H from X times [0,1] to Y with endpoints f and g
questions.explanation: A homotopy is a continuous deformation parameterized by the unit interval.

questions.prompt: What is the fundamental group of the circle S1?
options: A two-element cyclic group
The integers under addition
The trivial group
The real numbers under multiplication
questions.answer_text: The integers under addition
questions.explanation: Winding number identifies homotopy classes of based loops in the circle with integers.

questions.prompt: For a path-connected space, what does simply connected require?
options: Every based loop is null-homotopic
Every open set is connected
Every continuous map is invertible
Every covering is nontrivial
questions.answer_text: Every based loop is null-homotopic
questions.explanation: Simply connected means path connected with trivial fundamental group.

questions.prompt: What is an evenly covered neighborhood for p:E to B?
options: An open U whose preimage is always one point
A closed subset on which p is constant
A neighborhood requiring a metric isometry
An open set U whose preimage splits into sheets mapped homeomorphically onto U
questions.answer_text: An open set U whose preimage splits into sheets mapped homeomorphically onto U
questions.explanation: Local sheet decompositions characterize covering maps.

questions.prompt: Given a covering map and a path with a chosen initial lift, how many lifted paths exist?
options: Infinitely many regardless of the start
One for each point in the base
Exactly one
None for all paths
questions.answer_text: Exactly one
questions.explanation: Path lifting exists uniquely once the initial point in the fiber is fixed.

questions.prompt: What is the fundamental group of a contractible nonempty space?
options: Always non-Abelian
Trivial
Always the integers
Always finite nontrivial
questions.answer_text: Trivial
questions.explanation: Contractibility supplies a homotopy collapsing every loop.

questions.prompt: In a chain complex, what identity must consecutive boundary maps obey?
options: The composition of two boundaries is zero
Every boundary map is invertible
Every cycle is a boundary
The boundary of every chain is nonzero
questions.answer_text: The composition of two boundaries is zero
questions.explanation: The chain-complex axiom is boundary squared equals zero.

questions.prompt: What is H0 of a nonempty path-connected space with integer coefficients?
options: Zero
The rational numbers modulo integers
Two copies of the integers
The integers
questions.answer_text: The integers
questions.explanation: H0 has one integer generator per path component.

questions.prompt: What is the first singular homology of the circle with integer coefficients?
options: Two copies of the integers
The cyclic group of order two
The integers
Zero
questions.answer_text: The integers
questions.explanation: The circle has one independent one-dimensional cycle.

questions.prompt: What is the Euler characteristic of the two-dimensional sphere?
options: Minus 2
questions.explanation: A standard cell structure has one zero-cell and one two-cell, giving 1+1=2.

questions.prompt: For a finite two-dimensional simplicial complex, what is Euler characteristic?
options: Vertices minus edges plus faces
Vertices plus edges plus faces
Edges minus vertices only
Faces divided by edges
questions.answer_text: Vertices minus edges plus faces
questions.explanation: Euler characteristic is the alternating count of cells or simplices.

questions.prompt: What does homology classify in degree k?
options: All k-dimensional open subsets
Only smooth charts
Only metric distances
k-dimensional cycles modulo k-dimensional boundaries
questions.answer_text: k-dimensional cycles modulo k-dimensional boundaries
questions.explanation: The kth homology group is kernel of the boundary map modulo image of the next boundary map.

questions.prompt: A coordinate chart on an n-manifold maps an open neighborhood homeomorphically to what?
options: A single point
An arbitrary closed subset of Euclidean space
An open subset of n-dimensional Euclidean space
The entire tangent bundle
questions.answer_text: An open subset of n-dimensional Euclidean space
questions.explanation: Charts supply local Euclidean coordinates.

questions.prompt: What condition makes overlapping manifold charts smoothly compatible?
options: Every chart preserves Euclidean distances
Transition maps are smooth where defined
Chart images have equal areas
Charts share the same coordinate origin
questions.answer_text: Transition maps are smooth where defined
questions.explanation: Smooth atlases require smooth changes of coordinates.

questions.prompt: Which description of a tangent vector at p is mathematically valid?
options: A derivation on germs of smooth functions at p
A point of the manifold without extra structure
An arbitrary non-linear operator
A globally constant coordinate vector only
questions.answer_text: A derivation on germs of smooth functions at p
questions.explanation: Derivations satisfying the Leibniz rule model tangent vectors.

questions.prompt: For a smooth map f:M to N, what is df at p?
options: The inverse of f on all points
A set of unrelated directional scalars
A metric on N
A linear map from the tangent space at p to the tangent space at f(p)
questions.answer_text: A linear map from the tangent space at p to the tangent space at f(p)
questions.explanation: The differential sends tangent vectors forward linearly.

questions.prompt: Which conditions define a diffeomorphism?
options: A map preserving just connectedness
A linear map between any two manifolds
A smooth bijection with smooth inverse
A continuous surjection only
questions.answer_text: A smooth bijection with smooth inverse
questions.explanation: Both the map and its inverse must be smooth.

questions.prompt: What kind of object is the Lie bracket of two smooth vector fields?
options: A metric tensor of rank two
A smooth vector field
A scalar constant independent of location
A coordinate chart
questions.answer_text: A smooth vector field
questions.explanation: The commutator of derivations is again a derivation and hence a vector field.

questions.prompt: If F from Rn to Rk has rank k at a zero, what does the regular-level-set theorem give locally?
options: A smooth submanifold of dimension n minus k
A submanifold of dimension n plus k
A discrete space regardless of n
No local geometric structure
questions.answer_text: A smooth submanifold of dimension n minus k
questions.explanation: Surjective derivative gives a local regular level set of codimension k.

questions.prompt: What makes y a regular value of smooth f:M to N?
options: Every preimage point is critical
The target must have dimension zero
The preimage must contain exactly one point
Every derivative at a point of its preimage is surjective
questions.answer_text: Every derivative at a point of its preimage is surjective
questions.explanation: Regularity requires surjective differentials at all preimage points.

questions.prompt: If f from R5 to R2 has derivative of rank 2 along the level set, what is the level-set dimension?
questions.explanation: Regular level sets have dimension 5 minus 2.

questions.prompt: What does Sard's theorem say about critical values of a sufficiently smooth map?
options: They are all regular values
They form a measure-zero subset of the target
They fill every open set
They always form a finite set
questions.answer_text: They form a measure-zero subset of the target
questions.explanation: Sard's theorem gives measure zero for the set of critical values under the standard smoothness hypotheses.

questions.prompt: When do embedded submanifolds A and B meet transversely at p?
options: Their tangent spaces together span the ambient tangent space
Their tangent spaces coincide in every case
They intersect at exactly one point
Both have zero curvature
questions.answer_text: Their tangent spaces together span the ambient tangent space
questions.explanation: Transversality is the tangent-space span condition.

questions.prompt: For a regular value of a smooth map between compact oriented manifolds of equal dimension, how is degree calculated?
options: Number of preimages without signs in all cases
Total area of the target
Dimension of the kernel of every differential
Sum of local orientation signs at preimage points
questions.answer_text: Sum of local orientation signs at preimage points
questions.explanation: Degree counts signed preimages at a regular value.

questions.prompt: For a regular parametrized curve r(t), what is its speed?
options: The norm of r(t)
The torsion
The Euclidean norm of r'(t)
The curvature of the curve
questions.answer_text: The Euclidean norm of r'(t)
questions.explanation: Speed is the magnitude of the velocity vector.

questions.prompt: For a circle of radius R greater than zero, what is its curvature?
options: R divided by 2
1 divided by R
R squared
questions.answer_text: 1 divided by R
questions.explanation: A circle has constant curvature equal to the reciprocal of its radius.

questions.prompt: Which integral computes arc length of a smooth regular curve on [a,b]?
options: The integral from a to b of the norm of r'(t) dt
The integral of r(t) without a norm
The difference r(b) minus r(a)
The integral of torsion alone
questions.answer_text: The integral from a to b of the norm of r'(t) dt
questions.explanation: Arc length integrates instantaneous speed.

questions.prompt: For a regular parametrized surface r(u,v), what spans its tangent plane?
options: Only the surface normal
The position vector alone
The Gaussian curvature
The two partial derivatives r_u and r_v
questions.answer_text: The two partial derivatives r_u and r_v
questions.explanation: Independent parameter derivatives span the tangent space.

questions.prompt: What are the coefficients of the first fundamental form?
options: Euler characteristic and genus
Only torsion and curvature
Dot products E=r_u dot r_u, F=r_u dot r_v and G=r_v dot r_v
Only three second derivatives
questions.answer_text: Dot products E=r_u dot r_u, F=r_u dot r_v and G=r_v dot r_v
questions.explanation: The induced surface metric is determined by dot products of tangent derivatives.

questions.prompt: What is Gaussian curvature of the round sphere of radius R?
options: R cubed
1 divided by R squared
Minus 1 divided by R
questions.answer_text: 1 divided by R squared
questions.explanation: Both principal curvatures have magnitude 1/R, so their product is 1/R squared.

questions.prompt: What property must a Riemannian metric have at each tangent space?
options: Positive-definite symmetric bilinear form
Alternating nondegenerate two-form
Arbitrary non-linear map
Only a distance function with no tensors
questions.answer_text: Positive-definite symmetric bilinear form
questions.explanation: A Riemannian metric assigns an inner product to each tangent space.

questions.prompt: What uniquely characterizes the Levi-Civita connection?
options: Nonzero torsion and no metric compatibility
Flatness on every manifold
Curvature equal to one
Metric compatibility and zero torsion
questions.answer_text: Metric compatibility and zero torsion
questions.explanation: The fundamental theorem of Riemannian geometry gives a unique metric-compatible torsion-free connection.

questions.prompt: What is the intrinsic differential equation for an affinely parametrized geodesic?
options: Its speed must be zero
Its Gaussian curvature is constant
Its tangent vector has zero covariant derivative along itself
Its ordinary Euclidean second derivative always vanishes
questions.answer_text: Its tangent vector has zero covariant derivative along itself
questions.explanation: A geodesic satisfies covariant acceleration equal to zero.

questions.prompt: In Cartesian coordinates on Euclidean space, what are the Levi-Civita Christoffel symbols?
options: Undefined
All zero
All one
All equal to the dimension
questions.answer_text: All zero
questions.explanation: The Euclidean metric coefficients are constant in Cartesian coordinates.

questions.prompt: What is sectional curvature of ordinary Euclidean space?
options: 1 everywhere
Minus 1 everywhere
Undefined for all dimensions
questions.explanation: Flat Euclidean space has identically zero Riemann curvature.

questions.prompt: How is Riemannian distance defined on a connected manifold?
options: Maximum curvature on any path
Euclidean coordinate distance in every chart
Volume of the shortest path
Infimum of lengths of piecewise-smooth curves joining the two points
questions.answer_text: Infimum of lengths of piecewise-smooth curves joining the two points
questions.explanation: The intrinsic distance minimizes curve length in the infimum sense.

questions.prompt: What is a differential two-form?
options: A vector field
A coordinate function
An alternating covariant rank-two tensor field
A symmetric metric tensor only
questions.answer_text: An alternating covariant rank-two tensor field
questions.explanation: Differential forms are alternating multilinear covariant fields.

questions.prompt: What is the square of the exterior derivative on differential forms?
options: The Hodge star
Zero
Identity
The Laplacian
questions.answer_text: Zero
questions.explanation: The exterior derivative satisfies d composed with d equals zero.

questions.prompt: What does generalized Stokes' theorem relate?
options: Integral of dω over M to integral of ω over the oriented boundary of M
Two arbitrary volume integrals
Integral of curvature to dimension alone
Length of a curve to its endpoints only
questions.answer_text: Integral of dω over M to integral of ω over the oriented boundary of M
questions.explanation: Stokes relates an exact derivative integral to the boundary integral.

questions.prompt: Which implication is always valid for differential forms?
options: Closed implies exact on every manifold
Every form is exact
No nonzero form is closed
Exact implies closed
questions.answer_text: Exact implies closed
questions.explanation: If ω=dη then dω=d²η=0.

questions.prompt: What is first de Rham cohomology of the smooth circle over real coefficients?
options: A two-dimensional real vector space
The integers as a real vector space
A one-dimensional real vector space
Zero
questions.answer_text: A one-dimensional real vector space
questions.explanation: A circle has one independent closed one-form class modulo exact forms.

questions.prompt: For one-forms α and β, which identity is correct?
options: Wedge products are ordinary scalar addition
α wedge β equals minus β wedge α
α wedge β equals β wedge α universally
α wedge α is generally nonzero
questions.answer_text: α wedge β equals minus β wedge α
questions.explanation: Alternation gives graded anticommutativity for one-forms.

questions.prompt: What does local triviality of a rank-k vector bundle mean?
options: Locally its total space is a product of an open base set with Rk
It must be globally a product
All fibers have dimension zero
The base must be finite
questions.answer_text: Locally its total space is a product of an open base set with Rk
questions.explanation: Bundles are locally products even when globally twisted.

questions.prompt: For an n-dimensional smooth manifold, what is the fiber dimension of its tangent bundle?
options: 2n
1 regardless of n
n
questions.answer_text: n
questions.explanation: The tangent bundle fiber at p is T_p M of dimension n.

questions.prompt: What makes a Lie group a Lie group?
options: A space with no differentiable structure
A manifold with no algebraic operation
Smooth group multiplication and inversion on a smooth manifold
A finite group only
questions.answer_text: Smooth group multiplication and inversion on a smooth manifold
questions.explanation: Lie groups combine compatible smooth and group structures.

questions.prompt: What does a connection on a vector bundle provide?
options: A preferred basis of every fiber automatically
A rule for covariantly differentiating sections along vector fields
A numerical curvature value without derivatives
A global trivialization in all cases
questions.answer_text: A rule for covariantly differentiating sections along vector fields
questions.explanation: Connections differentiate sections in a manner compatible with the bundle.

questions.prompt: What determines parallel transport of a vector along a smooth path?
options: The chosen connection
The topology alone without any connection
The Euler characteristic alone
A coordinate system with no additional data
questions.answer_text: The chosen connection
questions.explanation: Parallel transport solves a covariant differential equation set by a connection.

questions.prompt: What does curvature of a connection measure?
options: Only the number of charts
The size of the underlying set
Always zero by definition
Failure of covariant derivatives to commute after correcting for the vector-field bracket
questions.answer_text: Failure of covariant derivatives to commute after correcting for the vector-field bracket
questions.explanation: Curvature is encoded by the commutator of covariant derivatives minus the derivative along the bracket.

questions.prompt: What is a nondegenerate critical point of a smooth function?
options: Any local maximum regardless of Hessian
A point with zero-dimensional tangent space
A critical point with invertible Hessian
A point at which the derivative never vanishes
questions.answer_text: A critical point with invertible Hessian
questions.explanation: Morse nondegeneracy means the Hessian at the critical point is nonsingular.

questions.prompt: What does the Morse index count at a nondegenerate critical point?
options: Number of charts
Negative eigenvalues of the Hessian, with multiplicity
Positive eigenvalues only
Connected components of the manifold
questions.answer_text: Negative eigenvalues of the Hessian, with multiplicity
questions.explanation: The index is the dimension of a maximal negative-definite subspace.

questions.prompt: For a closed oriented surface, what is the total Gaussian curvature?
options: 2π times its Euler characteristic
Always zero
Always 4π regardless of topology
Surface area squared
questions.answer_text: 2π times its Euler characteristic
questions.explanation: Gauss-Bonnet equates integrated Gaussian curvature to 2πχ.

questions.prompt: What does Poincare-Hopf relate for a vector field with isolated zeros on a compact oriented manifold?
options: The sum of local indices to total volume
Only curvature to length
Every index to the dimension exactly
The sum of local indices to Euler characteristic
questions.answer_text: The sum of local indices to Euler characteristic
questions.explanation: Poincare-Hopf identifies the index sum with the Euler characteristic.

questions.prompt: What is the Euler characteristic of a torus?
options: Minus 2
questions.explanation: For a genus-one closed orientable surface χ=2-2g=0.

questions.prompt: What does the hairy ball theorem prohibit on the two-sphere?
options: A nonzero normal vector field
A continuous nowhere-zero tangent vector field
Any continuous function
Any smooth embedding into Euclidean space
questions.answer_text: A continuous nowhere-zero tangent vector field
questions.explanation: The sphere has nonzero Euler characteristic; tangent fields must vanish somewhere.

questions.prompt: What does persistent homology track in a filtered family of complexes?
options: Birth and death of homological features across filtration parameters
Only the number of original data points
Only Euclidean distances without topology
Only connected graphs at a single scale
questions.answer_text: Birth and death of homological features across filtration parameters
questions.explanation: Persistence follows homology classes as the filtration grows.

questions.prompt: In a Vietoris-Rips complex at scale ε, when is a finite vertex set a simplex?
options: Exactly one edge is present
The points have zero pairwise distances
The vertices lie on a straight line
Every pair of its vertices is connected at threshold ε
questions.answer_text: Every pair of its vertices is connected at threshold ε
questions.explanation: The Rips complex is the clique complex of the distance-threshold graph.

questions.prompt: Which evidence is essential for a reproducible computational topology experiment?
options: Only the reported answer
A citation without a method
Data provenance, parameters, code version, and independent checks
A screenshot without inputs
questions.answer_text: Data provenance, parameters, code version, and independent checks
questions.explanation: Reproducibility requires enough information to independently repeat the computation.

questions.prompt: If two spaces are homeomorphic, what must agree?
options: Their volumes in every metric
Their Euler characteristics when defined
Their exact Euclidean distances
Their ambient embedding dimensions
questions.answer_text: Their Euler characteristics when defined
questions.explanation: Euler characteristic is a topological invariant for appropriate finite-type spaces.

questions.prompt: For a connected closed orientable surface of genus g, what is Euler characteristic?
options: 2 minus 2g
2 plus 2g
g squared
One divided by g
questions.answer_text: 2 minus 2g
questions.explanation: The classification of surfaces gives χ=2-2g.

questions.prompt: What turns a numerical picture into a defensible research claim?
options: An attractive visualization alone
A single random trial claimed universal
A citation without checking assumptions
A clear theorem with checked hypotheses or a precisely limited computational conclusion
questions.answer_text: A clear theorem with checked hypotheses or a precisely limited computational conclusion
questions.explanation: Valid research separates theorem-level proof from evidence for a limited numerical observation.

diagnostic.prompt: The negation of “for every x there exists y with P(x,y)” is…
options: there exists x such that for every y, not P(x,y)
for every x and y, not P(x,y)
there exists y such that every x satisfies P
P is false once
diagnostic.explanation: Negation reverses each quantifier and negates the predicate.

diagnostic.prompt: To prove A=B, the standard elementwise method is…
options: prove A⊆B and B⊆A
compare one example
compare cardinalities only
assume equality
diagnostic.explanation: Mutual inclusion proves set equality.

diagnostic.prompt: A map f is injective when…
options: f(x)=f(y) implies x=y
every codomain point has a preimage
f is continuous
domain and codomain have equal size
diagnostic.explanation: Injectivity means distinct inputs cannot share an output.

diagnostic.prompt: A metric must satisfy…
options: nonnegativity, identity, symmetry and triangle inequality
linearity and differentiability
compactness
orientation
diagnostic.explanation: These are the metric axioms.

diagnostic.prompt: A sequence is Cauchy when…
options: late terms become arbitrarily close to one another
it has a stated limit from the beginning
it is monotone only
its first terms are close
diagnostic.explanation: The Cauchy condition compares sufficiently late terms.

diagnostic.prompt: The derivative dF_p of F:R^m→R^n is represented by…
options: the Jacobian matrix at p
the Hessian always
a truth table
an open cover
diagnostic.explanation: The Jacobian is the coordinate matrix of the differential.

diagnostic.prompt: The rank-nullity theorem states…
options: dim V=rank T+nullity T
det T=trace T
rank T=dim W always
kernel and image are equal
diagnostic.explanation: Rank-nullity decomposes domain dimension.

diagnostic.prompt: The inverse function theorem requires…
options: an invertible derivative at the point
compact domain only
a group action
a zero derivative
diagnostic.explanation: An invertible derivative gives a local diffeomorphism.

diagnostic.prompt: A continuous function on a compact interval…
options: attains a maximum and minimum
must be differentiable
must be injective
has zero integral
diagnostic.explanation: The extreme-value theorem applies.

diagnostic.prompt: The chain rule for smooth maps is…
options: d(F∘G)=dF∘dG
d(FG)=F+G
d²=1
rank(F∘G)=0
diagnostic.explanation: Differentials compose in the same order as maps.

diagnostic.prompt: A group homomorphism satisfies…
options: φ(ab)=φ(a)φ(b)
φ(a+b)=φ(a)+b for every structure
φ is automatically bijective
ker φ is empty
diagnostic.explanation: It preserves the group operation.

diagnostic.prompt: A quotient by an equivalence relation consists of…
options: equivalence classes
only singletons
open sets only
tangent vectors
diagnostic.explanation: The quotient set contains equivalence classes.

diagnostic.prompt: A proof by contradiction begins by…
options: assuming the negation of the target
assuming the target
checking examples only
drawing a diagram
diagnostic.explanation: The negated conclusion is used to derive impossibility.

diagnostic.prompt: A compact subset of R^n is characterized by…
options: closed and bounded
open and bounded
connected and dense
finite only
diagnostic.explanation: Heine–Borel gives the Euclidean characterization.

diagnostic.prompt: The gradient of f points in the direction of…
options: steepest increase
zero curvature always
the tangent to every level set
decreasing dimension
diagnostic.explanation: The gradient is normal to regular level sets and gives steepest increase.

diagnostic.prompt: A regular level set F⁻¹(c) requires…
options: dF to have full rank along the level set
F to be constant everywhere
the domain to be finite
every point to be critical
diagnostic.explanation: The regular-value condition gives a submanifold.

diagnostic.prompt: The determinant of a change-of-basis matrix controls…
options: orientation and volume scaling
compactness
connectedness
homotopy class alone
diagnostic.explanation: Its sign and magnitude encode orientation and volume scaling.

diagnostic.prompt: A line integral of a 1-form depends on…
options: the form and the oriented path
only the endpoints in every case
only the path length
the ambient dimension alone
diagnostic.explanation: Path independence requires extra hypotheses such as exactness.

diagnostic.prompt: The boundary of a boundary identity is…
options: ∂=differentiation
∂X=X
diagnostic.explanation: This identity underlies chain complexes and homology.

diagnostic.prompt: Mathematical software output is…
options: evidence that must be interpreted and verified
a replacement for theorem hypotheses
automatically a proof
independent of input assumptions
diagnostic.explanation: Computation supports but does not replace proof.

diagnostic.prompt: Which practice is required when working with open-set axioms?
options: A rigorous response about open-set axioms states the definition, verifies every hypothesis, distinguishes local from global claims, and supplies a proof or justified computation.
A picture alone establishes the theorem.
One successful example proves a universal statement.
Definitions may be chosen after the calculation.
diagnostic.explanation: A rigorous response about open-set axioms states the definition, verifies every hypothesis, distinguishes local from global claims, and supplies a proof or justified computation.

diagnostic.prompt: Which practice is required when working with closed-set complements?
options: A rigorous response about closed-set complements states the definition, verifies every hypothesis, distinguishes local from global claims, and supplies a proof or justified computation.
